title: High-resolution Millimeter Imaging of the CI Tau Protoplanetary Disk: A Massive Ensemble of Protoplanets from 0.1 to 100 au
question: What is the continuum structure of the CI Tau disc at high resolution, and can its annular gaps be explained by massive planets accompanying the hot Jupiter?

evidence.quote: in our emissivity modeling adopt the temperature profile derived by (cite: Kwon)
by comparing our $1.3$mm flux with the $2.7$mm measurements of (cite: Guilloteau2011)

recipe.method: envelope plus three logistic gaps, fitted to visibilities with GALARIO and emcee

recipe.goal: Hydrodynamic modelling of gaps with planets
recipe.method: 2D FARGO3D with dust, synthetic emissivity compared to fitted profile, then synthetic image via CASA ft and CLEAN
key_parameters: alpha=0.014, disc mass 20 MJ within 200 au, 350x512 cells, 5.6-378 au
assumptions: fragmentation velocity 10 m/s; dust-to-gas 0.01; a^-3 size distribution of compact silicate grains

evidence.quote: three prominent annular gaps at radii $\sim$ 13, 39 and 100 au
planets of mass 0.75, 0.15 and 0.4 $M_\mathrm{Jupiter}$ are located at orbital radii of 14, 43, and 108 au
A spectral index of $2.9 \pm{} 0.35$ is derived

answer_key.quantity: Upper limit flux ratio inside/outside innermost gap

evidence.quote: upper limit on the ratio of the flux inside to outside the gap of $\sim 0.28$

not_stated_but_needed: Cell size, image size, masks, CLEAN threshold
Cleaning/imaging details of the modelling visibilities (averaging, any self-calibration)
Details of the dust opacity table and temperature profile
Flux calibrator and flux scale uncertainty
score_reason: Fitting method and parameters are well documented, but imaging details and hydro setup are partial.
